Q: Excel VBA - parse JSON string and set cell values based on key:values A:

This code can process the sample data

Sub processjson()

inpstring = Range("H1")
i = 1
colcount = 1
rowcnt = 1
Do While InStr(i, inpstring, ":") <> 0
    If colcount = 5 Then colcount = 1: rowcnt = rowcnt + 1
    Cells(rowcnt, colcount) = Mid(inpstring, InStr(i, inpstring, ":") + 2, InStr(InStr(i, inpstring, ":") + 2, inpstring, """") - InStr(i, inpstring, ":") - 2)
    i = InStr(InStr(i, inpstring, ":") + 1, inpstring, Chr(10)) + 1
    colcount = colcount + 1
    
Loop

End Sub

For testing purpose the input is in cell H1.
The resulted processed data are in columns A:D from row 1.
When you use it, can make a parameter for the Sub, with the variable name inpstring and then of course remove the assignment to it. Sub processjson(inpstring As String)

Q: RegEx search in Chrome network requests tab A:

Try wrapping your expression with /, e.g. use:

/(set_session_email|get_session_email|send_sync_info|send_sync_purchase_info)/

Q: Exception “Could not find template with id” after upgrading Microsoft Information Protection SDK from 1.15.104 to 1.17.x A:

The workaround is to turn off the "offline publishing" introduced in 1.17.137. Update MipConfiguration.FeatureSettingsOverride.

FeatureSettingsOverride = new()
{
  [FlightingFeature.FileSDKOfflinePublishing] = false
};

Version 1.17.137

Release Date: June 9, 2025

File SDK

  • Added support for EML file types.

  • Added support for offline publishing.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/information-protection/develop/version-release-history#version-117137

I did not managed to make it work with offline publishing. The example does not compile, because the methods does not exist and it does not work out of the box as advertised.

Using Offline Publishing with the File SDK

The File SDK uses offline publishing by default and requires no additional setup or configuration.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/information-protection/develop/concept-offline-publishing#net-example

Q: How do I run a program with a different working directory from current, from Linux shell? A:

Using GNU coreutils [1] to run a command in a modified working directory:

$ pwd ; env -C / pwd ; pwd
/tmp
/
/tmp

For the specific question:

$ find /a /b /c
/a
/a/helloworld
/b
/c

$ cd b
/b $ env -C /c ../a/helloworld 

/b $ find /a /b /c
/a
/a/helloworld
/b
/c
/c/hello-world.txt

/b $ cat /a/helloworld 
touch hello-world.txt

[1] https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/env-invocation.html
